conversation.content:
Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to experience a wide range of emotions during this time, and I'm here to support you.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential areas of concern. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource in our postpartum care. By taking a few minutes to go through this assessment, we can get a better sense of your emotional well-being and make sure you're receiving the support you need during this important time.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential and respected. My goal is to create a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings without any judgment. I'm here to listen and help in any way I can.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

Let's get started. I'd like to begin by asking: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

To be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle. I mean, I still find some things funny, like my baby's little antics, but it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it takes a lot more effort to find the humor in things. I do still enjoy some activities, like watching my baby sleep or playing with her, but even those things don't bring me as much joy as they used to. It's like everything feels a bit dulled, you know? I'll catch myself smiling or laughing at something, but it's not as deep or as frequent as it used to be. Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I don't think I have, not as much as I used to, anyway. Like I said, it's just harder to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm so worried about everything, especially my baby's safety, that it's hard to let my guard down and just laugh. And when I do laugh, it feels a bit forced, you know? Like I'm trying to convince myself that everything is okay, but deep down, I'm still feeling really anxious and overwhelmed.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just felt like too much effort. Even things that I used to enjoy, like spending time with friends or trying new restaurants, just don't seem as appealing to me right now. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, you know? Taking care of the baby and keeping everything together is just so exhausting, and it's hard to muster up the energy to think about doing anything else. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, and I'll get a little spark of excitement, but it's quickly overshadowed by feelings of anxiety and guilt. Like, I'll think about leaving the baby with my husband and going out with friends, but then I'll start worrying that something will happen to the baby while I'm away, or that I'm a bad mother for wanting to take a break. It's just hard to enjoy anything when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and guilty all the time.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, unfortunately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already questioning every decision I make, and when things don't go exactly as planned, I can be really hard on myself. Like, if the baby is fussy and I'm having trouble soothing her, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm her down?" or "I'm a terrible mother for not knowing how to do this." It's like I'm constantly second-guessing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. And even when things are going okay, I'll still find ways to criticize myself. For example, if I'm feeling tired and I need to take a nap, I'll think, "You're so lazy, you should be using this time to clean the house or do laundry instead of sleeping." It's like I'm always looking for ways to blame myself, even when things aren't really my fault. It's exhausting, to be honest.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something that might happen to her. Like, I'll think, "What if she chokes on something?" or "What if she gets sick?" or "What if something happens to me and I'm not there to take care of her?" It's like my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I can feel my heart beating faster and my stomach getting all knotted up. And the thing is, there's no reason for me to be thinking these things. The baby is healthy, and I'm doing everything I can to take care of her. But my mind just won't stop worrying. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll wake up to check on the baby, not because I've heard her cry or anything, but just because I'm worried that something might be wrong. It's like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something bad to happen. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm always "on" and can't relax, even when everything is fine.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. Like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no actual threat there. It's just me, the baby, and the quiet of the house. And it's so scary, because I don't know what's happening or why I'm feeling that way. Sometimes it's triggered by a thought, like I'll think about the baby getting hurt or something, and then I'll start to feel panicky. But other times, it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll feel this overwhelming sense of fear. It's like my mind is playing tricks on me, and it's really hard to calm myself down when it happens. I've tried taking deep breaths, and trying to focus on the present moment, but it's hard to shake the feeling of panic once it's started. And it's not just the panic itself, it's the fear of losing control, of not being able to take care of the baby, that's really terrifying.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly running on empty, and I don't have any energy left for anything else. Even simple tasks, like laundry or cooking dinner, feel like they're too much for me to handle. And it's not just the physical tasks, it's the emotional weight of being a new mom too. I feel like I'm responsible for this tiny human's entire well-being, and that's a really heavy burden to carry. Sometimes I just feel like I'm drowning in it all, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of overwhelm, like I'm just not cut out for this mom thing. And that's a really scary feeling, because I want to be a good mom, I want to be able to take care of my baby, but sometimes it feels like everything is just too much for me.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Even when she's sleeping, I'll lie awake for hours, just feeling anxious and unhappy. My mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, or all the things I'm not doing right as a mom. And it's hard to shake those thoughts, you know? They just keep replaying in my head, over and over again. Sometimes I'll get out of bed and check on the baby, just to make sure she's okay, but even when I see that she's sleeping peacefully, I still can't seem to calm down. And then, when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up a few hours later, feeling exhausted and anxious all over again. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of unhappiness and worry, and I don't know how to break free from it. Some nights, I'll wake up and just cry, because I feel so overwhelmed and alone. And it's hard to explain, because from the outside, everything looks fine. The baby is healthy, my husband is supportive... but on the inside, I just feel like I'm struggling to keep my head above water.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really feeling the joy or happiness that I thought I would. Most days, I just feel sad and overwhelmed. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. It's like the sadness just washes over me, and I don't know how to stop it. Sometimes it's triggered by something, like a difficult feeding session or a sleepless night, but other times it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be doing okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness and hopelessness. It's like I'm grieving the life I had before the baby, or the person I used to be. I know that's not rational, because I love my baby and I'm grateful to be her mom, but it's hard to shake the feeling that I've lost myself in all of this. And it's hard to talk about, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy and grateful all the time, but the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I don't know how to make it better. Sometimes I'll have moments where I feel okay, where I'll laugh or smile, but they're fleeting. The sadness and misery always seem to come back, and it's exhausting.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the tears are just always there, waiting to spill out at any moment. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not always because something specific is wrong, it's just that the emotions are so overwhelming. I'll cry because I'm tired, or because I'm feeling anxious, or because I'm just feeling so much pressure to be a good mom. Sometimes I'll cry because I'm feeling guilty about something, like not being able to breastfeed, or not being able to soothe the baby's cries. And sometimes I'll cry just because I'm feeling so alone, like I'm the only one who's struggling with all of this. It's hard to explain, but it's like the tears are just a release of all the emotions that are building up inside of me. I've cried in front of my husband, and he's always trying to comfort me, but even his comfort can't always stop the tears. I've cried in the shower, or while I'm driving, or just sitting in my room, feeling overwhelmed. It's like my body is just releasing all the stress and anxiety that I've been carrying around, and it's exhausting. I wish I could just stop crying, but it's like my body is trying to tell me something, like I need to acknowledge all these feelings and emotions that I've been trying to suppress.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

.. (pausing, looking down) Yes... I have had those thoughts. They're scary and overwhelming, and I don't know how to make them stop. It's like, sometimes I'll be feeling so anxious and sad, and I'll just think, "What's the point of all this? Why am I even here?" And then, these thoughts will creep in, like, "Maybe it would be easier if I just wasn't here anymore." It's not that I really want to harm myself, it's just that the pain and the sadness feel so overwhelming, and I don't know how to escape it. It's like, my mind is just trying to find a way out, but it's not a healthy way out. (starting to tear up) I'm scared of those thoughts, because I don't want to act on them. I want to be a good mom, and I want to be here for my baby. But sometimes, when the darkness feels like it's closing in, I don't know how to keep those thoughts at bay. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I know it sounds crazy, but it's just how I've been feeling lately. (looking up, with tears in my eyes) I'm sorry. I don't know why I'm saying all this. It's just... it's hard to keep it inside.

2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if experiencing suicidal thoughts

4. Support patient in developing coping strategies and stress management techniques
5. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities and prioritize sleep hygiene practices
